title: About
text:
Researcher · University of Cyprus  Yobsan Bayisa Leta .   PhD Student / MSCA Doctoral Researcher    BASED IN  Nicosia, Cyprus        KIOS Research and Innovation Center of Excellence University of Cyprus Nicosia, Cyprus                            Making vision models more reliable in the world beyond the benchmark.  I am a PhD student at the  University of Cyprus , conducting research at the  KIOS Research and Innovation Center of Excellence . As part of the  TIRAMISU MSCA Doctoral Network , I study robust and efficient neural networks for edge AI.  My research connects  computer vision, robust deep learning, and neural architecture search . I am particularly interested in semantic segmentation under adverse conditions, and in models that balance accuracy with the memory, energy, and latency constraints of edge devices. title: Projects
text: Code & applications  Projects  Independent applications, tools, and resources from my GitHub repositories. Code accompanying papers is linked from Publications.    View my GitHub        5 projects  Search projects       Research resources                  Evolutionary multiobjective neural architecture search   Paper collection · Benchmarks · Taxonomy · Updated 2026-10-03  A curated research collection covering evolutionary methods for discovering neural architectures that balance predictive performance with latency, energy, memory, and model complexity. It connects research papers with code, benchmarks, and deployment considerations.   GitHub      Documentation        Project details  The collection organizes the field around search spaces, search strategies, objective functions, evaluation strategies, and techniques for accelerating search. It also covers hardware-aware design, robustness, emerging applications, and reproducible evaluation.       Applied machine learning                  Telecom bandwidth forecasting and anomaly detection   Python · LSTM · Jupyter · Updated 2026-08-27  Time-series models for forecasting data-centre traffic and identifying unusual bandwidth patterns. LSTM forecasters use recent traffic history to predict future samples, while an LSTM autoencoder flags windows with unusually high reconstruction error.   GitHub      Documentation        Project details  Separate workflows cover univariate forecasting, multivariate forecasting, and anomaly detection. Shared preprocessing uses chronological train-test splits and training-only scaling. Forecasts are evaluated against a persistence baseline with MAE, RMSE, and R².       Applied machine learning                  Telecom alarm classification   Python · BERT · TextCNN · Updated 2026-08-27  A language-model pipeline for organizing short Chinese telecom alarm reports into meaningful categories. It first discovers groups through sentence embeddings and clustering, then trains a BERT classifier to assign new alarms to those groups.   GitHub      Documentation        Project details  The project supports multiple category counts, includes a character-level TextCNN baseline, and provides notebooks and command-line tools for clustering, training, and prediction. Evaluation includes per-class reports, confusion matrices, and a majority-class baseline.       Computer vision                  5G-V2X roadside perception system   Python · PyTorch · ONNX · Updated 2026-08-27  A roadside perception pipeline that detects and tracks road users, maps detections into road coordinates, estimates collision risk, and shares scene information with nearby vehicles. It brings vision, tracking, and communication together in an edge system.   GitHub      Documentation        Project details  The repository includes object detection, semantic segmentation, Kalman-filter tracking, camera calibration, optional camera-radar fusion, and versioned messages over UDP. A virtual onboard unit supports local testing; physical C-V2X communication requires a vendor-specific transport integration.       Probabilistic modeling            Visualizing Gaussian process regression   Python · scikit-learn · Jupyter · Updated 2026-08-23  A notebook exploration of how covariance kernels shape Gaussian process predictions on weather observations. Visualizations compare predicted temperatures with measurements and show the uncertainty associated with each prediction.   GitHub      Documentation        Project details  The notebook defines Rational Quadratic, periodic, Matérn, RBF, and combined kernels. It uses scikit-learn’s GaussianProcessRegressor to estimate predictive means and standard deviations, alongside regression error metrics. Its random holdout evaluates interpolation rather than a chronological forecasting task.      No projects match this search. Try vision, telecom, or Gaussian.

title: LiDSeg: Linear DehazeFormer Guidance for Efficient Semantic Segmentation in Adverse Weather Conditions
text: LiDSeg adds a lightweight guidance encoder to semantic segmentation models for adverse weather. Auxiliary image reconstruction supports training; at inference, the reconstruction decoder is removed while the guidance encoder and gated fusion remain. The framework supports multiple segmentation backbones and evaluation across fog, rain, snow, and night conditions. Yobsan Bayisa Leta Christos Kyrkou Maria K. Michael Theocharis Theocharides

text: A curated research collection covering evolutionary methods for discovering neural architectures that balance predictive performance with latency, energy, memory, and model complexity. It connects research papers with code, benchmarks, and deployment considerations. The collection organizes the field around search spaces, search strategies, objective functions, evaluation strategies, and techniques for accelerating search. It also covers hardware-aware design, robustness, emerging applications, and reproducible evaluation. Paper collection · Benchmarks · Taxonomy

title: Telecom bandwidth forecasting and anomaly detection
text: Time-series models for forecasting data-centre traffic and identifying unusual bandwidth patterns. LSTM forecasters use recent traffic history to predict future samples, while an LSTM autoencoder flags windows with unusually high reconstruction error. Separate workflows cover univariate forecasting, multivariate forecasting, and anomaly detection. Shared preprocessing uses chronological train-test splits and training-only scaling. Forecasts are evaluated against a persistence baseline with MAE, RMSE, and R². Python · LSTM · Jupyter

title: Telecom alarm classification
text: A language-model pipeline for organizing short Chinese telecom alarm reports into meaningful categories. It first discovers groups through sentence embeddings and clustering, then trains a BERT classifier to assign new alarms to those groups. The project supports multiple category counts, includes a character-level TextCNN baseline, and provides notebooks and command-line tools for clustering, training, and prediction. Evaluation includes per-class reports, confusion matrices, and a majority-class baseline. Python · BERT · TextCNN

title: 5G-V2X roadside perception system
text: A roadside perception pipeline that detects and tracks road users, maps detections into road coordinates, estimates collision risk, and shares scene information with nearby vehicles. It brings vision, tracking, and communication together in an edge system. The repository includes object detection, semantic segmentation, Kalman-filter tracking, camera calibration, optional camera-radar fusion, and versioned messages over UDP. A virtual onboard unit supports local testing; physical C-V2X communication requires a vendor-specific transport integration. Python · PyTorch · ONNX

title: Visualizing Gaussian process regression
text: A notebook exploration of how covariance kernels shape Gaussian process predictions on weather observations. Visualizations compare predicted temperatures with measurements and show the uncertainty associated with each prediction. The notebook defines Rational Quadratic, periodic, Matérn, RBF, and combined kernels. It uses scikit-learn’s GaussianProcessRegressor to estimate predictive means and standard deviations, alongside regression error metrics. Its random holdout evaluates interpolation rather than a chronological forecasting task. Python · scikit-learn · Jupyter
